problem:
Which of the following determinants are equal to $0?$

$$
|A|=|\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & \sqrt{3} \\ \sqrt[5]{2} & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|B|=|\begin{aligned}1 & \sqrt{2} & 4 \\ 0 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}|,\,|C|=|\begin{aligned}1 & \sqrt{2} & 4 \\ 2 & 3 & 8 \\ 1 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}|
$$

activity_context.topic_title: Conditions When a Determinant Equals Zero

feedback.worked_solution:
Let's examine each matrix in turn.

- For the matrix $A,$ we have

$$
det(A)=2\sqrt{2}\cdot \sqrt{2}-1\cdot 1=3.
$$

- Since $B$ has proportional columns, we obtain

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}1 & \sqrt{2} & 2 \\ 2 & 1 & 4 \\ 3 & 6 & 6\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,det(B)=0.
$$

Therefore, $4det(A)+4det(B)=4\cdot 3+4\cdot 0=12.$
